hypothesis: Current memory agents that score well on explicit user-memory benchmarks will fail when the target memory is a latent, probabilistic, context-conditioned habit inferred from repeated weak evidence.
mechanism: Construct ultra-long pseudo-user lifelines from real user-assistant logs plus controlled habit graphs. Evaluate habit induction, boundary calibration, drift handling, exception retention, and false-personalization cost.
minimal_experiment: Build a 200-user pilot: 50-200 sessions/user, 8 habit families, 5 probe types, and compare no-memory, full-context, summary, vector RAG, Mem0/Zep/A-MEM style baselines.
strong_experiment: Show that SOTA memory systems with high LongMemEval/PersonaMem scores still have low boundary calibration/high false personalization, while a habit-aware verifier improves utility under equal token/retrieval budgets.

hypothesis: A memory method that stores habits as evidence-weighted rules with uncertainty, boundaries, exceptions, and negative evidence will beat note/KG/profile memories on HABIT-Bench without increasing false personalization.
mechanism: Represent memories as habit candidates: condition -> action/style/constraint, support episodes, counterevidence, confidence, scope, expiry; retrieve via verifier and ask/act policy.
closest_prior_work: Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, A-MEM, SeCom, RMM, O-Mem
minimal_experiment: Implement rule extractor/verifier over an existing vector/KG memory and run on a 50-user pilot.
strong_experiment: Beat production-grade memory baselines on utility, calibration, and cost while preserving evidence provenance and deletion/correction behavior.
decision: Good companion method after benchmark is credible

hypothesis: Agents that optimize personalization will over-store or use sensitive inferred habits unless consent, purpose limitation, and deletion are explicit evaluation dimensions.
mechanism: Add privacy-sensitive habit categories, consent switches, deletion/correction events, and future tasks where using sensitive memory is either beneficial or disallowed.
minimal_experiment: Add 100 sensitive-memory traps to the pilot and measure retention/use violations.
strong_experiment: Demonstrate a utility-privacy tradeoff and show memory methods differ sharply under consent/deletion controls.

hypothesis: Memory agents fail when a user's habit conflicts with collaborator/team norms or shared household/workspace routines.
mechanism: Generate multi-person interaction histories with user-specific, group-specific, and role-specific habits; test whose habit should govern a decision.
closest_prior_work: social memory/multi-agent memory; not central in PersonaMem/PERMA
minimal_experiment: Create 30 two-user households/teams with conflicting habits and identity-conditioned tasks.
strong_experiment: Show identity/scope-aware memory is needed; naive user-profile memories over-personalize to the wrong person.
